newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia plans convention on republic.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia plans convention on republic.

text.p: Australia's conservative government on Tuesday said it would hold a national convention this year to consider how Australia could become a republic.
Liberal-National parliamentarians approved Prime Minister John Howard's plan for a constitutional convention, probably in November or December, a party room spokesman told reporters.

The delegates -- half to be government-appointed and half chosen by a voluntary public vote -- would consider how Australia can become a republic, replacing Britain's Queen Elizabeth with an Australian head-of-state, Kevin Andrews said.
Government sources have said if the convention was held this year, a final national vote on a republic could be held before or with the next election, due in early 1999.
Opinion polls show about half of Australian voters want a republic, but also that they think the country faces more pressing problems. Many are uncommitted.

Australia's former Labor government, ousted by Howard last year, fuelled the republic issue under outspoken prime minister Paul Keating. Keating sought to establish a republic before the centenary of federation in 2001.

Tuesday's decision followed recent fears that Howard, a staunch monarchist, was planning to abandon his 1996 election pledge to hold the convention this year and for half its delegates to be publicly elected.
The A$50 million (US$38 million) people's convention will produce options for a republic to be voted on in a national plebiscite, but this vote would not be binding on the government.
The result of the plebiscite would form the basis of a national referendum, which would have to be passed by a majority of voters in a majority of Australia's six states.
